new_method:
To ensure genuine novelty, we propose an enhanced version of RAFM that introduces a meta-learning based noise adaptation mechanism and explicit feature disentanglement. In this refined method, called Meta-Disentangled Robust Adaptive Fusion (M-DRAF), the process is modified as follows:

• Meta-Learned Noise Adaptation: In addition to the dynamic filtering module, a meta-learner is incorporated to rapidly adapt to unseen and heterogeneous noise types. This meta-learner is trained to predict optimal filtering parameters based on the current noise profile, learning a mapping from noise statistics to filter configurations in a few-shot manner. This goes beyond simple unsupervised clustering by enabling fast adaptation to novel noise conditions.

• Explicit Feature Disentanglement: The multi-stage feature extraction is extended by disentangling noise-specific and content-specific features. A dedicated adversarial branch is introduced where a discriminator encourages the separation of noise patterns from underlying content. This disentangled representation is then used in the dual training strategy, ensuring that only the noise-invariant parts contribute to the downstream task while the noise-specific components are suppressed.

• Cross-modal Consistency Regularization: To further improve robustness, the refined method leverages cross-modal consistency regularization (using, e.g., auxiliary modalities or simulated noise patterns) that enforces consistency between noise-reduced features across different augmentations. This helps in stabilizing the feature fusion process in highly variable environments.

This refined method not only addresses the noise sensitivity issues of the Base Method but also introduces a novel meta-learning framework and explicit feature disentanglement that represent significant departures from existing approaches in the literature.
